links.outcome: Fact precision and hallucination rate of grounded multi-agent RAG versus non-grounded baselines
links.effect: MA-RAG increased Fact Precision up to 122% (0.436 to 0.990) and reduced Hallucination Rate by up to 98% (0.564 to 0.010) versus Traditional, RAG-only, and Single-agent RAG baselines.
links.quote: Compared to Traditional, RAG-only, and Single-agent RAG baselines, MA-RAG substantially improves factual correctness, achieving up to a 122% relative increase in Fact Precision (from 0.436 to 0.990) and reducing the Hallucination Rate by up to 98% (from 0.564 to 0.010), while consistently receiving top ratings from clinical experts for organization and clinical usefulness.

unlisted_practices: Multi-agent decomposition with domain-specialized agents and a final verification stage for query-driven summarization of longitudinal structured assessment data

screen.reason: Evaluates a novel multi-agent RAG framework (MA-RAG) for summarizing longitudinal Parkinson's disease data using automated metrics and clinical expert evaluation, but evaluates a novel system architecture rather than a health system deployment practice.
